title: GLP-1R endpoint role classification — preregistered rules
question: After honestly separating functional agonism from binding affinity, does Genesis hold enough scientifically appropriate GLP-1R rows to train an activity model under the EXISTING frozen gate?
author: Claude, for Mariusz (mariusz8789-sudo)
scope: GLP-1R (CHEMBL1784) only. This is a per-campaign classification for an agonist question. It is NOT a policy for other targets and does NOT change how any other campaign selects endpoints.

disclosureBeforeFreezing.why: Preregistration is worthless if it hides what was already seen. Everything below was observed BEFORE this file was frozen.
observed: The backend pin packages/backend/src/campaign/glp1rActivity.json holds 287 rows, 214 distinct canonical SMILES, 25 distinct assayIds, and no assayDescription column.
standardType distribution in the pin: EC50 194, IC50 89, KI 4.
data/transcription/glp1r-a3/*.psv holds 90 transcribed ChEMBL assay records with descriptions; 9 of the pin's 25 assayIds are covered there, 16 are not.
The descriptions of those 9 assays were read.
scripts/glp1r-d144-expanded.mjs admits A1 rows only when the assay appears in A3, so every A1-sourced row in the D-144 combined set has a description.
notObservedBeforeFreezing: The per-role row counts, compound counts and scaffold counts that this preregistration is written to produce.
Any classification of the A1-sourced rows.

assayDescriptions.provenance: ChEMBL assay records, hand-transcribed with per-row custody (D-105/D-108), columns: assayId | targetId | assayType | bao | format | description
assayDescriptions.note: ChEMBL was not reachable from this container (ebi.ac.uk denied). No description was fetched, inferred or written by Genesis.

activityRows: data/transcription/glp1r-a1/*.psv restricted exactly as scripts/glp1r-d144-expanded.mjs admits them (the D-144 combined set)

classificationRules.appliedTo: each distinct assayId, never to an individual row
inputsAllowed: the A1 actionType field where present
inputsForbidden: standardType alone — an EC50 is NOT evidence of agonism by itself
anything not present in a cited source

roles.FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM: the description states agonist activity (or the row carries actionType AGONIST) AND names a readout in the Gs/cAMP arm: cAMP accumulation/production/level, or a reporter gene explicitly driven by cAMP. Both conditions required.
roles.OTHER_FUNCTIONAL: a functional receptor readout that is NOT the Gs/cAMP arm (beta-arrestin recruitment, receptor internalization, calcium mobilization), or allosteric modulation (PAM/NAM), or antagonism.
roles.BINDING_AFFINITY: displacement, competition or saturation binding of a labelled ligand; Ki or Kd determination.
roles.UNKNOWN: no description available (reason BLOCKED_BY_DATA_ACCESS), or a description that names no readout and no mechanism (e.g. bare "potency" or "effective concentration"), or signals that conflict.

classificationRules.tieBreak: Any assay that does not unambiguously satisfy exactly one role is UNKNOWN. Guessing is forbidden. An assay is never promoted to FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM because its standardType is EC50.
classificationRules.speciesFlag: The receptor is recorded as human only where the description says human (or the row's target resolves to CHEMBL1784 with no contrary statement). A description saying 'unknown origin' sets speciesStated=false. This is recorded, never silently corrected.
classificationRules.systemFlag: Every assay here is a recombinant heterologous expression system (CHO, HEK293, BHK, COS7, 9-3-H). That is recorded and is NOT evidence of native human tissue pharmacology.

deduplicationRule.rowIdentity: (moleculeId, assayId, standardType) — as already enforced when the D-144 combined set is built
deduplicationRule.modellableUnit: distinct canonicalSmiles within one role; a compound measured in several assays of the same role counts once toward compound count
deduplicationRule.rowCountForGate: rows remaining in the role after row-identity deduplication, since the existing gate counts rows

scaffoldRule.method: Bemis-Murcko scaffold via RDKit MurckoScaffold on the canonical SMILES
scaffoldRule.note: Reported as a diagnostic. The production pipeline computes its own scaffold through packages/backend/src/compute/rdkitAdapter.mjs; this count is independent and is labelled as such.

sufficiencyCriterion.gateReferenced: packages/backend/src/campaign/glp1r-validation-gate.json, ruleFingerprint d2f77a7e6042f0fc, UNCHANGED by this work
sufficiencyCriterion.SUFFICIENT: FUNCTIONAL_AGONISM rows >= 190 AND distinct scaffolds >= 20 AND a scaffold-disjoint split can place >= 150 rows in train and >= 40 in test
sufficiencyCriterion.INSUFFICIENT_FUNCTIONAL_DATA: any of the above not met
sufficiencyCriterion.consequence: On INSUFFICIENT_FUNCTIONAL_DATA, D-145 ends. No model is trained, no gate is altered, no threshold is relaxed, no row is dropped to make a number work, and no ranking is produced. That verdict is a complete and valid result.

forbidden: editing glp1r-validation-gate.json or any sealed artefact
changing the split after seeing any result
excluding rows for any reason not written in this file
re-running the classification with different rules to obtain a different count
treating a docking score, an EC50 or an expression datum as evidence of agonism
outputs: packages/backend/src/campaign/glp1r-assay-roles.json — one entry per assayId with role, evidence quote, source and flags
